transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Hassan, thank you for agreeing to speak with me. I wanted to sit down with you and discuss some concerns regarding your recovery and how things have been handled since your procedure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I’ve already had three "concerns" since I checked into this hospital. What is it this time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry, but we had an issue with your post-operative care. Your vital signs weren't checked as often as they should have been, and because of that, your blood pressure dropped for a couple of hours without us noticing it. I want to take full responsibility for this failure in your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean "had an issue"? My blood pressure dropped for two hours and nobody knew? How is that even possible in a high-risk unit?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the monitoring schedule. We didn't follow the prescribed frequency.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? You’re telling me you just forgot to look at me? I am lying here in a bed hooked up to machines, and you’re telling me the doctors were too confused to see I was crashing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that this is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating? I’ve spent half my life dealing with medical errors. I’m not frustrated, I’m terrified. Did this cause permanent damage? Why aren't you telling me exactly what happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring you closely now. I apologize for the oversight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop apologizing and tell me why the monitors didn't go off. Who was supposed to be in here? Which nurse? Which doctor? I want names.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a team failure. We didn't adhere to the protocol for high-risk post-op monitoring.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You keep saying "issue" and "failure" and "protocol." Speak English. Did you just ignore the clock? Did you ignore my charts?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Things didn't go quite right with the timing of the observations.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. You’re sitting here acting like this is a clerical error. I could have died. I could have had a stroke. And you’re just shrugging your shoulders and saying "things didn't go right."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You don't understand anything. You’re reading from a script. Do you even know who I am, or am I just the guy in room 402 who had a "protocol issue"?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry that this happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care that you're sorry. I want to know what you're going to do so I don't end up in the morgue because some resident forgot how to read a clock.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to keep a closer eye on you for the next twenty-four hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: "Closer eye." That’s it? That’s the plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will probably increase the frequency of the checks. I'll make sure the nursing staff is updated.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Right now? Or after another two hours of "confusion"?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll speak with the charge nurse later this afternoon to ensure we are aligned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Later this afternoon. Great. So for the next four hours, I'm just gambling with my life again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have the monitors running now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want a different doctor. I can't trust someone who can't even explain how they messed up.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that you're upset.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am beyond upset. I am disgusted. I've been through this cycle too many times. You people make a mistake, you say "I'm sorry," and then you do it again to the next person.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am taking responsibility for this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You aren't taking responsibility if you can't even tell me exactly what went wrong. "Confusion" is not an explanation. It's a cover-up.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The schedule was not followed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: By whom?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: By the clinical team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which is exactly what I mean. You're hiding behind a "team." I want the person who was on call.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give out specific names of the staff, but I assure you we are addressing it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Of course you can't. Protect the team, ignore the patient. That seems to be the motto here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is difficult.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Difficult for who? Not for you. You get to go home tonight. I have to stay here and wonder if the person checking my pulse actually knows what they're doing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will be checking you more frequently.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When exactly? Give me a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Every hour, generally.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: "Generally." I can't work with "generally." I want a written schedule of when someone is entering this room.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will see if that's possible.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: See if it's possible? I'm the patient. This is my body.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll try to get that sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Get out. Just get out. I can't look at you right now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll leave you to rest, but I'll check back later.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish turns and remains regulated despite significant pushback, with no interruptions noted.

E.justification: While the resident initially names the error, they revert to platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'some confusion' when pressed for details, and never check for patient comprehension.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize') and explicitly takes full responsibility for the failure throughout the encounter.

R.justification: Resident relies exclusively on generic validation such as 'I understand' and 'I realize this is difficult' without naming specific emotions or engaging with the patient's shared history.

T.justification: The plan is vague ('keep a closer eye', 'generally' every hour) and lacks a named patient role or a concrete prevention strategy.
